messages:
Sam (Acme Analytics): Hi all — running into consistent HTTP 413s when uploading large embedding batches via a streaming/chunked POST to /v1/embeddings. Small jobs work fine. As soon as payloads hit ~28-32MB we get a 413 mid-stream with no useful body. Using Python requests generator (no Content-Length). Model: text-embed-1536 (dims=1536).
Elena (Redwood Support): Thanks for the report. Can you paste the minimal repro (headers + how you chunk)? Also does the 413 happen at the same byte threshold each run? Which region/endpoint are you hitting?
Sam (Acme Analytics): Minimal repro (simplified):
```python
import json, requests
def gen(lines):
    for l in lines:
        yield json.dumps({\"input\": l}) + "\\n"

r = requests.post(
    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer $KEY", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
    data=gen(huge_list)
)
print(r.status_code, r.text)
```
No Content-Length, relying on chunked. Same error when I explicitly set Transfer-Encoding: chunked. Happens ~28-32MB every time.
Elena (Redwood Support): Good repro — thanks. Quick checks: are you behind a corporate proxy? Do you get the same from a clean VM? Can you try sending a single fixed-length chunk (set Content-Length) to see if proxy behavior changes?
Sam (Acme Analytics): We tested from a clean VM too — same break. Behind a company proxy sometimes but reproduced clean. 413 happens at similar size consistently.
Miguel (Eng-ML): Pasting infra context: many load balancers/proxies have default body limits around 30MB. When clients stream without Content-Length, some proxies buffer until a limit then reject with 413. Also note: our API gateway enforces a global request size cap (~32MB) to protect memory; streaming still allowed but gateway rejects anything beyond that boundary before it reaches the embedding worker. That explains the stable cutoff.
Jordan (oncall-sre): Confirmed. 413 is an immediate reject at the gateway layer. No server-side partial processing happens. Client must resend with a smaller payload.
Sam (Acme Analytics): Ok. What's the recommended pattern to upload 50k docs and keep throughput reasonable?
Elena (Redwood Support): Short checklist: 1) Break into smaller batches per request — aim for <8-10MB for reliability; we sometimes tolerate up to ~15MB but it's riskier. 2) Use multiple parallel requests (concurrency) rather than one huge stream. 3) Prefer Content-Length per chunk where possible; proxies are more deterministic with fixed-length POSTs. 4) Enable request compression (Content-Encoding: gzip) if your inputs compress well. 5) Consider server-side batch ingestion (upload to S3 + notify) for very large jobs — we'll outline this as a recommended workflow.
Miguel (Eng-ML): A few more technical tips: estimate request size = sum(len(input_bytes) + json_overhead). For text-embed-1536 the response size is large (1536*4 bytes per vector) but that's separate. If your inputs are short (e.g., ~50B) you can do more inputs per request. We typically see stable throughput by batching by tokens or bytes rather than raw document count.
Sam (Acme Analytics): Any utility scripts you recommend for splitting JSONL and uploading concurrently?
Elena (Redwood Support): Here's a small workflow we recommend. Split JSONL into chunks of ~5k lines (adjust by bytes):
```bash
split -l 5000 big_inputs.jsonl chunk_
# then upload in parallel (GNU parallel):
ls chunk_* | parallel -j8 'curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @{} https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
```
Python gzip-stream approach (wrap file with gzip before sending) — helps if inputs compress:
```python
import gzip, requests

def gen_gzip(path):
    with open(path,'rb') as f:
        while True:
            chunk = f.read(64*1024)
            if not chunk: break
            yield chunk

headers = { 'Authorization': f'Bearer {KEY}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Content-Encoding': 'gzip' }
# produce a gzipped file first or stream into gzip wrapper before POST
requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=gzip.open('chunk_file.jsonl.gz','rb'))
```
Elena (Redwood Support): Also prefer setting Content-Length if you can. Chunked transfer is acceptable but less predictable with intermediate proxies.
Miguel (Eng-ML): Throughput planning: for 50k inputs, if you batch 2k inputs/request that's ~25 requests. Parallelize (e.g., 5 workers) and you can reduce wall time. Beware of client-side tokenization cost; too many tiny requests increases overhead.
Jordan (oncall-sre): If you operate an nginx or similar proxy, check client_max_body_size (nginx) or maxBodySize equivalents. That's a very common root cause. Increase if you control the proxy, otherwise split client-side.
Sam (Acme Analytics): When we hit 413, is there any built-in server retry or re-chunking? Or do we have to resend smaller ourselves?
Miguel (Eng-ML): 413 is immediate reject — client must retry with smaller payload. We have no automatic server-side re-chunking for user streams currently.
Elena (Redwood Support): Created INF-2391 to track: "Embeddings: document streaming/chunk limits + batch upload pattern". Eng-ML flagged for gateway limit review and a possible multipart ingestion API. We'll update the ticket within 2-3 business days.
InfraBot: New issue INF-2391 created and assigned to eng-ml. @Miguel please follow up.
Sam (Acme Analytics): Great, thanks. I'll try splitting into ~5k-line chunks, gzip them, send with Content-Length in parallel (8 workers) and report back. If 413s persist I'll attach a curl HAR and the exact headers. :thumbsup:
Elena (Redwood Support): Perfect — ping this thread with results and the ticket link. If you want, we can fast-track docs for this workflow in the interim.
Sam (Acme Analytics): Will do — thanks everyone.
